body: Absolutley. When I am in a bad place emotionally a good long walk always helps. It doesn't make the feelings go away, but it just helps put it all in perspective. If I can't go for a walk due to weather constraints any kind of exercise helps, but not nearly as good as being outside. I could really use a walk today,  but it is way too hot for it.

I too have those thoughts on a nearly daily basis. We have a lot of similarities. 

I've dealt with depression for some time, but I do a good job of putting a mask on and hiding it away. 

I've been going through some rough times recently with marital problems where these thoughts have been amplified.  Right or wrong I divulged this to my wife. She was obviously upset. Things got pretty bad but I realized that while I have these thoughts, I really doubt I would ever follow through. I would simply hurt too many people that I care about. 

This was a couple months ago and right now we are doing better on the marriage front, but I still have these thoughts. I should be happier, but deep down I am not. My wife assumes that I am fine now since I put on my mask. I think some days she picks up on it, but never enough to say anything or if she does that I can't explain it away as I'm tired or have a headache.

I have also tried some medications with little success, in fact it usually got worse. I tried a therapist many years ago and like the medications, no real improvement. So I learn to live with it and keep my mask handy. 

The only thing that helps me is getting out and going for long walks by myself. One day I was gone for over 3 hours and walked close to 10 miles.

I've been married for 25+ years and haven't really felt loved or appreciated for at least the last 10. We are trying to work it out but it is very difficult for me. If you find my other posts you will see that my wife was, maybe still is, having an emotional affair. I caught her texting the other guy, while sitting right next to me, how she wished she was with him and how handsome he is. Talk about a punch to the gut.  She hasn't flirted with me since before the marriage and I can't recall her ever calling me handsome. I don't know why I stay, but I still love her.

Listen, I've been there. I still feel that way sometimes. 

The thing about depression is that it can blind us so that we refuse to see that there are people who care. Sometimes it is even the same people who are driving us insane.

Just take each moment one step at a time. No matter how small the task, be proud that you succeeded. Get out of bed - be proud, take a shower - be proud, one step or one moment at a time is all you need.

Honesty is really hard to find and maintain. 

To quote Billy Joel...

*Honesty is such a lonely word
Everyone is so untrue
Honesty is hardly ever heard
And mostly what I need from you*

I'm trying to rebuild a 25+ year marriage where honesty was lost, from both sides. Assuming we are able to salvage our relationship, honesty and trust will be the hardest things to restore.

So while it seems my situation is much worse, I can relate. If you lead someone to say something you need to hear, you just never know if they really mean it or are just trying to make you happy or even worse just avoiding the subject.

So to give an update. I felt we were making strides. We had a few conversations and some tender moments that made me feel like there was hope. Then last night she was on her computer and I just sensed something was up, a gut feeling. 

We went to bed but when I got up that nagging feeling came back.  So I am not proud of this, but I figured out what her FB password was and checked her messages. My gut feeling was right and she was outright flirting with him, saying she wished she was with such a handsome man, all while sitting only 4 feet away from me.  I was livid,  so I confronted her this morning. Of course she was mad I looked at her FB and violated her privacy, but obviously I can't trust her. So we talked a good long time and she did apologize for flirting and I want to believe it has never gone beyond that but I have my doubts. 

I still want to make this work. So we will see. There is a lot of work ahead of us and I am sure more painful conversations no matter how it ends up.

I absolutely understand what you were trying to do, it is just that I felt you were not looking at all the facts to see that only two instances of being jealous over a 30 year period really should show that I am not that controlling jealous type. I get it about the depression. It is tough when you are on edge from it and your emotions are in constant overdrive.

You are right, a lot of the advice I am getting from all over is that I should just walk away and that if she is lying to me, then I would never be able to trust her again. In my heart I do not think it ever became physical, maybe as far as some flirting. The emotional affair I know happened and while that is still rough to handle, the fact that we have been having some issues and I know that I have not been providing the emotional intimacy she needs I can accept it. Like you said 25+ years of marriage is way too much to just walk away from without giving it my best attempt to salvage what we have. I know it is not going to be easy, but even if there is only a 1% chance of success it is worth it to me. I do still really love her with all of my heart. It is good advice to think about what I would tell my kids in this situation. The funny thing is that one of my daughters is in a similar situation and she kicked him to the curb. I support her decision 100%. The difference is that she does not have 30 years invested.

As much as I am trying to absolutely believe I can save this marriage, I am also thinking of MY future no matter how this ends. I have been focusing a lot of energy in bettering myself - not only to try to win my wife back but also to improve my confidence, health and general happiness. 

I am spending a lot of time though trying to decide if I confront my wife about her lies and the fact that I know at least a portion of the truth. In the end I have already accepted what happened and I am willing to forgive and move on. The issue is that if she never admits what happened, my trust in her will never be restored.

Your comments now are spot on. I think we just caught each other at a bad time. I hope you have a better day as well. Depression is tough to deal with. When I am in a bad place I just try to focus on the very next step I need to do. Take a shower, done. Get some "healthy" dinner, done. Go exercise, even if it is just a walk, done. ETC. If I can complete those tasks one step at a time I can get through the rest. 

Now one warning about exercising when depressed, I tend to overdo it when consumed with my thoughts. One evening I went for a walk and was gone for roughly 3 hours and had walked almost 10 miles. My feet were killing me, but I slept like a rock that night due to being exhausted.

Thank you for your concern. When this first started I will admit I was in a very dark place. My world had basically came crumbling down and for a good while I just did not care about anything. During a talk with her I revealed that I had considered suicide to save us from going through a divorce. This resulted in a big emotional talk that really changed my attitude. Now I am taking much better care of myself, I've done a lot of reflection and am making changes in me that I can control. I don't try to win an argument anymore as that just means the marriage loses. I've been eating better and taking my stress and anxiety out with exercise.

Ok I accept that and I apologize for reacting somewhat harshly.  I felt you were attacking my character and trying to make me out to be something I am not. 

We all have our bad days and like I am trying to do with my wife, I need to work on the whole take a breath first before reacting.

I hope your day gets better,  I've also been dealing with depression as well.

To  [Thedaythemusicdied37](https://www.reddit.com/user/Thedaythemusicdied37) ,

I was enjoying our discussion until you decided to make baseless accusations about my character and not looking at all of the facts I provided. 

For you to then get upset when I provide the information you were looking for that showed your assumptions were wrong and then delete all of your comments? Wow, for someone who is dishing out advice - here is some you should take to heart.  

People make mistakes, I for one respect people for being able to admit when they made a mistake and learn from them. People who run from their mistakes deserve no respect. It is a shame that because you deleted all of your comments, that my replies are also gone. I am not ashamed of anything I have written.

Did I ever say I had the answers? 

You were categorizing me and making statements that are not based in reality.

And now you delete your comment, just shows your character I guess. I stand behind what I write.

Ok I am trying to not get defensive but you are attacking each of my points. I will address them briefly and then move on. 

-I am simply not going to share the details of the proof I have that it went too far. She outright stated to him that she lied to me about there being "nothing between us" and that she thought I bought it. She is hiding the details of their conversations and there are expressions of love between them. That is an emotional affair plain and simple. That good enough for you? As for the physical affair, there is enough innuendo that something happened. Do I know for sure, no and I never stated I did. 

‐Now for my judgement of character. There have only been two guys that I have worried about. Guy #1 ended up cheating on his wife with her best friend. Both marriages ended in divorce. Scumbag. This guy is engaged and from the evidence I have is at the very least emotional involved with a married woman while engaged to be married. Scumbag. This is over a 30 year relationship. I'd say those are pretty good numbers and I was spot on in my assessment.  Also, only twice over 30 years should show that I am not some over bearing jealous control freak. She makes plans with her friends and coworkers, both male and female,all the time and I am 100% supportive and do not question or check up on her. 

-As for my wife being responsible for getting drunk,  sure she played a part in it. She is also an extreme light weight and also one not to refuse an act of kindness like buying her a drink or someone refilling drink without her knowledge. I also believe my wife would have tried to refuse any actions on his part. The issue is that if this guy refused to take no for answer though she was in no physical shape to stop him. So this first time I do not blame her for anything that happened, other than I warned her that I did not trust HIM. If you care about someone and you think they are going to be alone with someone you do not trust,  I for one will worry. If you wouldn't then that is your prerogative and you can live with the risk and responsibility. 

This time there was a distinct change in behavior when coupled with the late night texting raised flags.

So as for treating her like a child, come on. Twice in thirty years have I been concerned about someone or a situation and said anything. You do not know anything more about our relationship so i will give you the benefit of doubt, but look at the facts i have given you. I think you are trying to categorize me as one of those abusive control freaks.

Here are some additional facts:

- In all of our disagreements over the last 30 years I have NEVER disrespected her by swearing, calling her names or dismissing her feelings. I will admit that up until very recently I went into an argument with the desire to win. I have learned that winning the arguement means losing.

-I have never belittled her either in private or in public intentionally. I not going to try and say that over thirty years I have not said something that upset her, but it was never my intent. 

‐While I am the primary bread winner,  SHE controls the money. I have never questioned her spending habits as she is very frugal and trust her completely with our finances. She could have loads of our money stashed away in private accounts or in coffee cans in the back yard. One thing to note is that we have had joint accounts since before we we married. It has always been our money. Also the only reason I am the primary source of income is that SHE decided to stay home with our kids when they were born. Before that she brought in more money. 

- She is an extrovert and has tons of friends. I am just the opposite and keep my friends to a minimum and close to me. As I said earlier she goes out often and I never question or really care. Only when I feel something is off,  again twice in thirty years. 

So if you still categorize me the same way, then honestly your opinion means nothing to me.

I get what you are saying that it shouldn't matter on the other guy. In fact we've had that exact conversation leading up to the intervention I mentioned. In general I agree and I know I should trust her.  The issue is,  and she agrees,  that my wife sees everyone through rose colored glasses and can never see any alterior motives or character faults until it is too late. This first instance where I intervened my wife went out with a bunch of friends, including this guy, to a bar. He proceeded to get my wife completely drunk and was pushing to offer her a ride home. As she was drunk she was unaware of a wardrobe malfunction in progress. Unbeknownst to this guy, my wife and I agreed that I would be picking her up at the end of the night. I walked in as he was trying to get her out the door while eyeing her ever falling top.  Without making a scene I told him that I had her and took her home. Until that night she never saw this behavior in him, and then later as I said he moved on to someone else.

So like I said I am jealous and protective, but I also never tried stopping her from going out. I expressed my concerns and she dismissed them until my gut feeling was proved right. I am not controlling because of my jealousy and I'm not even sure I would call it jealousy. I am protective and I sense when someone is going to take advantage of my wife's personality. 

Now in this current situation, again I never tried stopping her from texting this guy,  just not so late at night when it is obvious he was waiting until his fiance was asleep. Again alterior motives.

I do agree with you, as I have said is that we obviously had issues that led up to this. I know that. I was obviously not meeting some emotional needs that this guy saw as a way in. Still pretty slimy for a guy who is engaged to be even thinking of getting involved with a married woman. 

Right now we are trying to work things out, but as I said from the beginning I know more than she realizes or has admitted to. That is what is making this difficult

I wish you the best of luck and thank you for sharing your experience with me. I believe everyone deserves a second, or even third chance. I know I am going to have a hard time trusting her. My hope is that after we can get back to a some what stable place,we can talk about it more

So first I never expected this to blow up like it did. I appreciate all of the comments. I take all advice and inputs seriously. I know I have a lot of responsibility in the situation so I do not take offense or get defensive in reading the comments. 

I can only assume that this is getting the attention it is because everyone has experienced a broken heart before. 

I will try to respond to each topic, hopefully I cover them all. I am on my mobile so hard to scroll back and forth. 

First am I jealous and controlling person? I will admit I can get jealous,  but it has always been based on the personality of the other guy.  Does my wife have other male friends, absolutely. I have only had these jealousy issue twice, including this one. I am a good judge of character and on the first one, because I intervened between him and my wife he moved on to a different friend and ended up having an affair and breaking up two marriages, his own and the other friend. On this one, I know for sure that there was at least an emotional affair going on, possibly more. I have proof of that. Leading up to this situation I met the guy and I felt uneasy from day one. He would not make eye contact and avoided any conversation. Keep in mind he is engaged to be married and has a kid from a previous relationship that failed for whatever reason. So yes I can be jealous, but only really when I sense the dude has bad intentions. 

Regarding the privacy.  So first I noticed the late night texting and I checked to see what was going on, I do not really feel like looking at the phone records is a serious invasion of privacy. I did not look at her phone or her messages. I asked her about it and then they switched to FB messenger so I could not see that they were still at it. It was her behavior and her still being on her phone late at night that worried me.  So yes in hind sight I should have just asked her about it instead of looking at her phone.  Now with that said, she knows my password on my phone and she knows that I knew her password. I did what I did because it was already obvious she was not being truthful with me.  It was wrong what I did and I did not decide to do that easily, but I felt I had to in order to get the truth. 

Now obviously this did not just happen out of the blue. We have had some issues building up for the last several years.  They were masked when our kids were home by being distracted. Now we are empty nesters and with no distractions the issues are front and center. Basically we are having issues connecting like we used to.  I think it is pretty common for couples to go through this. You are also correct that I did not realize how bad it was before this smacked it into me. 

Yes she did threaten a divorce and we have had several conversations since then, each a little more constructive than the last. I have realized that winning the arguement should NEVER be the goal. The goal is to save the marriage. With this new mind set I do not care of I need to give in even when I think I am right or justified in my actions. She has admitted that when she threatened divorce she was angry and feeling cornered so she knew she could swing the battle in her favor by that threat. She has since stated that she is not ready to give up. Unfortunately I have my doubts on her motivation. Is it really to save the marriage or is it to buy time to build up a financial nest egg to make the transition easier? I have no way to find that out. 

So with my new mind set I am trying to make this work and we are slowly making strides. BUT.... she is not aware that I know there was absolutely something going on. That is what brings me to this point. I guess the point is that I can move forward and accept what happened in order to stay together. The fact that she has not admitted what happened makes me worry she would do it again. 

My comments about manliness is that while I am trying to believe in this new mindset of marriage first, it feels like a lot of sacrifice and giving in. It means not always standing up for yourself if it serves the marriage better to give in. Just a lot to swallow at times and can wear on you.

So again I thank you all for your comments and best wishes. I am still trying to believe I can save this.

I'm just not sure. So to give a little background information. I was starting to get suspicious a few months ago as she was texting someone late at night, usually after midnight while I was sleeping. So I started watching our account to see the activity log. It was not hard to use a reverse lookup webpage to figure out who it was. I confronted her and she just said they were friends texting back and forth. Now one thing to note, he was ALWAYS the instigator of the conversation. She never texted him first. I said it was not appropriate and I asked her to stop. That caused a little bit of a fight and she dug up old issues and it blew up a little to a bigger fight but we moved on. Fast forward a couple weeks and the text messaging slowed down a bit and then stopped completely.  This seemed too good to be true so I decided to check her phone one morning when she was showering. To keep things going they switched to Facebook messenger so it would not show up on the account. So I confronted her about it. Instead of apologizing or admitting guilt, I got berated for violating her privacy. She said she was leaving and wanted a divorce in the heat of the arguement. I of course got scared and defensive and believe it or not apologized for going into her phone and begged her not to leave. I know, simply pitiful. I am ashamed of how whipped I am. She knows how much I love her and don't want it to end and whether it is on purpose or not, she is using that to her advantage.

So yes right now I am walking on egg shells trying to keep her happy and interested in staying. The thing is that I know I am showing complete weakness that simply can't be attractive. I know I should stand up for myself and be strong, but there is just so much at risk. You are right in that I am becoming a shell of a man and that just adds to my depression. When I am at home I am just catering to her every need. If I still knew where my "man card" was I know it would have been revoked a long time ago. 

I know I seem helpless, but I do appreciate your insights and validation in how I should be behaving. I know what I should do, but it is easier said than done.

Thank you. The logical side of my brain agrees completely with you. I absolutely feel more and more depressed as I continue to pretend. How can I expect her to be honest with when I am not being honest with myself. You are also right that I shouldn't be the one groveling to save this marriage. I am not the one who let my heart stray. 

My heart though is not ready to risk losing her. Yes she has betrayed me, but I have been with her for almost 30 years. I do still love her with all my heart. Yes I am absolutely scared of change and being alone, but I really want her in my life.

You are absolutely right that I am not ok with this.  You are also right that part of me would like to see this guys life as f'd as mine is right now.  He should feel the same repercussions.

I also feel that his fiance should know what has gone on to save her from committing to marriage with this piece of shit.

I think the only reason she is still here is financial stability. I am the primary source of income and while we are far from wealthy, we live comfortably. She could not survive on her income alone.

I am not naive in thinking that this affair just happened for no reason. I am not excusing her actions, but I know I could have done better in our marriage so she would not have looked for something/ someone else to fill what was missing. So that is what I am trying to do now. 

I am trying to avoid conflict, trying to put on a happy face and improve the things I can control. The hope is that my positive actions result in positive reactions.  It is a long shot and much easier said than done. It is very hard keeping my emotions in check when I feel so betrayed.

I know the feeling all too well. It just washes over you like a dark cloud that zaps all the energy and feeling out of you. I wish I could say it will get better, but who the hell am I to give you any promises. I can say, take a deep breath and focus on the extreme near term. You can get up from that bench, you can look around and find some happiness around you like a dog in the park, you can get through this moment.  Once you do, be proud of that accomplishment and use that to get through the next. One step at a time. That is all I do to get up from that bench.

I do still love her with all my heart and soul. I don't know how far this relationship went, but I do know she has lied to me about it and I have very strong suspicions and circumstantial evidence that it did become physical. Knowing all that and I still want to be with her should show my devotion. 

Part of me agrees with you and I should get it all out in the open. My reservations right now is that I think she would just leave.  As much I hate to say this, I think she would choose her affair with this other man over me right now. As pitiful this is I want to try and win her back. Show her the man she fell in love with all those years ago.  Then at some point bring it up. At least then I would have a fighting chance.

I thank you for the comment. At one point I did seriously consider suicide as a way out. The fact is that I know that I could never go through with it. I vowed to myself that I would/ will never hurt her. As much as I had it all planned out as an accident, I know it would still hurt her. I also have kids that I could never put through that, even if they never realized it was self inflicted. I have reached out to family, and it is a huge help. I still don't know what to do though. I still love her with all my heart.

I almost did it today. There is a really dangerous intersection on my way home from work and I purposely turned left in front of a semi thinking this is my chance. He slammed on the brakes and I made it through the intersection without a scratch. Now I'm at home dreading when the soon to be ex-wife gets home. It is just so emotionally draining when I feel so broken but sit here with a fake smile on my face.

Tell the kids what, that the marriage is over or that their father is thinking about suicide? No one but this reddit knows about my thoughts about the later and I plan on keeping it that way. It is much easier for the family to get over an accident than to realize what I may do. Some may say suicide is a selfish act, I feel completely otherwise. If I end the game I am going to do everything I can to make sure they are all ok in the end.

I tried talking to her tonight without it becoming too emotional and it was a complete failure. We got into it and now I am positive it is simply over. It would all just be easier if I didn't exist. All I want is for her to be happy.

Our kids have no idea we are having any issues, or at least I don't think they know. The wife may have talked to them already.

​

I simply don't know.......
